note: Adapted from Sjöstedt's (1900) description of the species; the original is in German. The alate is recorded as unknown in the original and no nymph is described; the measurements of total length and of head with mandibles in the soldier, and of body length and head width in the worker, are incomplete in the scanned text and are not recorded, while figure numbers, localities and collecting records are omitted.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head rectangular, sides straight and angles rounded in dorsal view, red-yellow; frons projecting forwards and upwards as a very pointed, setose process. Mandibles of peculiar shape, narrow, rod-like, toothless, almost straight in dorsal view, usually crossed, lying in front of the tip of the lingua; mandibles slightly longer than the head, curved downwards, slightly wider at the outer third, broad at the base and hollowed above; their apex very short, curved inwards. Antennae extending slightly beyond the apex of the mandibles, pale yellow with pale rings, 14-segmented, gradually longer towards the apex; basal segment thick, longer than the two following segments together, segments 3 and 4 small. Antennal sockets large. Labrum rectangular, with a small pointed projection at each anterior angle. Pronotum narrower than the head, anterior margin slightly concave at the middle; anterior and posterior lobes about equal in length.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head small, pale yellow; body elongate, very transparent in alcohol; frons behind the labrum white; head with a fine white line running from the middle to the antennal sockets and the occiput. First tooth of the right mandible distinct but scarcely larger than the second; first tooth of the left mandible only slightly larger, third tooth projecting as a small point, fourth tooth about as large as the first and rounded at the apex. Antennae 14-segmented, segments 3 and 4 about equal in length and shorter than the adjacent segments. Anterior margin of the pronotum forming a gentle arc, not concave at the middle.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Soldiers and workers were found together with soldiers and workers of Eutermes fuscotibialis in decayed wood.
